reasoning: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short at around 5 feet 2 inches is a well-documented historical misconception. Following his death on Saint Helena, Napoleon's autopsy recorded his height as "5 pieds 2 pouces" in pre-metric French units. Because a French inch (*pouce*) was longer than a British imperial inch (approximately 2.7 cm compared to 2.54 cm), 5 feet 2 inches in French measure converts to approximately 5 feet 6 inches to 5 feet 7 inches (168–169 cm) in standard modern measurements. In the early 19th century, the average height for an adult French male was around 5 feet 5 inches, meaning Napoleon was of average or slightly above-average height for his era. The perception that he was exceptionally short was largely popularized by British political propaganda (notably caricatures by James Gillray) and the confusion between French and imperial measurement systems.
